Laura — quick read-through and two candidate structures below. Numbers use a $100,000 list price (annual) to keep it simple; we can map back to Acme's PO amounts.

Option A (reseller visible commission) — customer sees itemized commission:
- List price: $100,000
- AWS marketplace fee (estimated): 5% = $5,000
- ResellCo commission (12% of list): $12,000 (line item)
- Redwood gross recognized pre-marketplace: $100,000
- Redwood net after marketplace fee and commission: $83,000
- Redwood records revenue: $95,000 if we invoice gross and marketplace remits fee separately OR records $83,000 if marketplace collects and remits net -- depends on billing flow.

Pros: transparent to Acme and ResellCo; commission appears on invoice. Cons: requires marketplace/invoice alignment.

Option B (gross-to-net settlement — simpler for marketplace):
- List price: $100,000 charged to customer by AWS
- AWS remits to Redwood after platform fee: assume AWS remits $95,000
- ResellCo receives a separate settlement from Redwood (12% of net or list? we should pick list-based commission for predictability — $12,000), leaving Redwood with $83,000 final cash.

Pros: cleaner invoice to customer (single line), easier marketplace settlement. Cons: less visibility for Acme unless we surface the breakdown in our renewal docs.

Tax handling — high level: for AWS Private Offers the tax treatment typically depends on the reseller/entity of record. Two common patterns:
- Reseller invoices and collects tax (ResellCo as merchant of record) — Redwood receives net settlement and does not collect tax on that invoice.
- Customer is billed by AWS (marketplace collects tax) and marketplace remits to taxing authorities; Redwood's settlement excludes tax.

Recommendation: propose Option B to Acme (AWS charges customer; AWS remits to Redwood; Redwood pays ResellCo commission via separate settlement). It reduces invoicing complexity for Acme and matches common marketplace flows.

I'll attach a quick workback (see channel_margin_workback_20271120.xlsx) with two tabs (Option A / Option B) and a short ops checklist for what ops needs to reconcile monthly.

If that sounds good I can draft the email back to Jane and Phil.

—Ben

Thanks — adding operational detail and a suggested checklist for legal/finance so we don't miss edge cases. Notes below (for Laura to send to Acme / ResellCo):

1) Revenue recognition / reporting: Redwood prefers to report gross ARR where we are the seller of record; where marketplace remits gross less fee, we need monthly remittance reports from AWS and a statement of gross charges to customer so our finance can reconcile. If ResellCo is merchant of record, Redwood should receive a written settlement schedule and proof of tax remittance.

2) Commission basis: For predictability use list-price-based commission (12% of list). If Acme requires commission of net after marketplace fee, be prepared for a lower dollar amount; document the rule in the SOW.

3) Tax/VAT: Add a clause — "Unless otherwise specified, taxes are handled by the marketplace or merchant of record. Parties will provide proof of tax remittance on request." This keeps Redwood insulated.

4) Ops checklist (to attach to the PO/email):
- Signed PO attached to the private offer ID
- Marketplace private-offer ID / SKU mapping confirmed
- Invoice flow documented (who receives invoice; who collects tax)
- Monthly settlement report from marketplace to Redwood (gross, marketplace fee, refunds)
- ResellCo settlement schedule and contacts
- Refund/credits handling: define which party issues customer credits and how Redwood gets reconciled credit for revenue reversals
- Rollover/renewal mechanics and how commission applies on renewal

5) Attach channel_margin_workback_20271120.xlsx and a one-page revenue allocation (I can draft).

I think Ben's Option B is operationally cleaner and safer for Acme. If Acme insists on an itemized commission on the invoice, it adds time to legal and the marketplace listing.

—Karthik

Hi Jane / Phil — thanks for the PO. Apologies for the slightly longer response — wanted to coordinate internally to give you clean options. Summary and recommendation below.

Summary (for a $100k list-price example):
- Preferred (Option B, marketplace flow): customer charged $100,000 by AWS; AWS takes a marketplace fee (estimate 5%) and remits to Redwood $95,000; Redwood pays ResellCo a 12% list-based commission ($12,000) via separate settlement, leaving Redwood with $83,000 cash.
- Alternate (Option A, itemized commission): commission shown as a line item on the invoice (12% = $12,000). This is fine but may require additional marketplace/invoice mapping and slow approval.

Tax handling: we recommend leaving tax collection to the marketplace or ResellCo as the merchant of record. If Acme prefers to be billed with tax shown, please tell us which entity will be collecting (AWS, ResellCo, or Acme) so we can align the private-offer billing config. We'll include a short clause in the SOW requiring proof of tax remittance if Redwood is not collecting directly.

Ops ask (what we need from you to finalize and push through procurement):
- Confirm you are OK with the marketplace (AWS) charging the customer and remitting to Redwood (Option B).
- Confirm ResellCo commission % (we used 12% here) or provide the exact rate you expect.
- Signed PO with private-offer ID (if available) or confirmation to proceed and we'll send the DocuSign link.

Next steps: If you confirm Option B and the commission rate, we'll:
1) Map the PO to the marketplace private-offer SKU and request the private-offer ID.
2) Circulate a short ops checklist and settlement cadence (monthly remittance + CSV).
3) Issue the DocuSign for the SOW and attach the revenue allocation appendix.

Attached are the PO (as you sent) and our channel margin workback that shows both options and the ops checklist for your finance team to review. If it helps, we can join a 30-min call with your procurement + ResellCo to walk through the flow.

If Phil / ResellCo want the commission shown on the invoice, flag it now — that will change the mapping slightly.
